frase_gancho.texto: Ninety-two objects from the sixteenth to the twentieth centuries, gathered to keep the religious art of all of Morelos.

puente_narrativo.texto: Follow your route: it may take you to the temple of the Third Order or to the Borda Garden.

guion_corto.texto: Ninety-two objects fit in this museum, which is small but concentrated. It is inside the cathedral and opened in two thousand eighteen. It gathers paintings, vestments and sculptures from the sixteenth to the twentieth centuries, all religious and viceregal art of Morelos. It was driven by the National Council Adopt a Work of Art, with the diocese, the INAH and the INBA, and the state government financed a good part. It is not the first attempt. In nineteen eleven, Bishop Francisco Plancarte y Navarrete founded another museum of sacred art in Cuernavaca. The cathedral’s collection includes paintings attributed to Juan Correa, Juan de Miranda and Tomás de Sosa. There is also a gilded wood relief from the eighteenth century about the stigmata of Saint Francis.

guion_largo.texto:
The words sacred art sound distant, but what is here is very close: objects that real people used to pray, celebrate and remember. The Museum of Sacred Art is inside the cathedral. It opened in two thousand eighteen as a worthy space to keep the religious and viceregal art of Morelos. Viceregal art is what was made when Mexico was New Spain.

It is a small museum, with around ninety-two objects: paintings, vestments and sculptures from the sixteenth to the twentieth centuries. Vestments are the cloths and objects that priests use in ceremonies. The figure may change over time, but it gives an idea of the scale: it is not an enormous gallery, but a selection.

The project was driven by the National Council Adopt a Work of Art, an organization that had already worked in the cathedral since the nineteen nineties. The diocese of Cuernavaca took part, along with the INAH and the INBA. Governor Graco Ramírez financed a large part of the project, according to the opening press release.

Cuernavaca had already had a museum like this. In nineteen eleven, the second bishop of the diocese, Francisco Plancarte y Navarrete, founded a Museum of Sacred Art. A researcher, María Celia Fontana, does not specify whether it was in the cathedral. What matters is the idea: for more than a century, the diocese wanted to gather and show its treasures.

What kind of works does the cathedral’s collection hold? Fontana mentions paintings attributed to Juan Correa, Juan de Miranda and Tomás de Sosa, artists of New Spain. There is also a polychrome and gilded wood relief from the eighteenth century, by an anonymous author. It represents the stigmatization of Saint Francis: the moment when, according to tradition, the saint received in his body the wounds of Christ. That relief closely resembles the one that adorns the portal of [the temple of the Third Order](cue_20_tercera_orden). We cannot guarantee which pieces are in the room today; it is worth asking at the entrance.

In nineteen ninety-two, several works from the cathedral were restored with the Adopt a Work of Art program, directed by Teresa Loera. That work prepared the ground for the museum.

Among the things to look at, notice how one saint is told apart from another. Each one usually carries an object that identifies him, such as a key, a palm or a book. Those attributes were the way of recognizing them from afar.

A question helps in looking at this kind of art: what was it made for? A painting of saints could teach stories to people who could not read. A vestment served at a feast. A sculpture was carried out in procession. When you think of it that way, sacred art stops being an object behind glass and becomes once again part of the life of a people.

texto: Find a painting with saints and ask what story it tells
Find a vestment and notice the cloth, the embroidery or the color
If there is a gilded wood relief, compare the figure with the portal of the Third Order

texto.Collection: 92 objects from the 16th to the 20th centuries, according to Lonely Planet
texto.Type of pieces: paintings, vestments and sculptures of the religious and viceregal art of Morelos
texto.Driven by: National Council Adopt a Work of Art, diocese, INAH and INBA
texto.Earlier museum: 1911, founded by Bishop Francisco Plancarte y Navarrete
texto.Authors cited in the cathedral’s collect: Juan Correa, Juan de Miranda and Tomás de Sosa

texto.pregunta: Myth: Sacred art is only for believers.
texto.respuesta: Reality: It can be looked at as history and as art. It shows how people painted, embroidered and sculpted in New Spain.
